title: Constructing mode-resolved quantum optical models for emitters in photonic crystals
authors: Antonio Morales-Pérez, Iñaki García-Elcano, Chiara Devescovi, Maia G. Vergniory, Aitzol García-Etxarri, Alejandro González-Tudela
abstract: Recent advances are enabling quantum emitters to interact with photonic crystals, whose electromagnetic modes exhibit complex dispersion relations, spatial mode structure, and polarization textures. However, modeling light-matter behavior in these systems faces a persistent trade-off: electromagnetic approaches based on Maxwell-equation solvers provide realistic vectorial descriptions but are difficult to integrate with quantum many-body and non-perturbative methods, whereas simplified quantum-optical lattice models are tractable but typically rely on scalar and spatially independent light-matter couplings that miss essential features of these structured photonic environments. Here, we introduce a constructive framework to derive quantum-optical lattice descriptions that overcome this trade-off. Combining symmetry-constrained tight-binding constructions with numerically computed photonic band structures and field profiles, our method yields minimal, symmetry-enforced lattice Hamiltonians that reproduce the target photonic dispersion while retaining the mode-resolved (position- and polarization-dependent) structure of the light-matter coupling. We show that these models recover Green's-function-based emitter dynamics in the perturbative regime, while providing access to non-perturbative quantum dynamical simulations beyond emitter-only descriptions. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to a two-dimensional photonic crystal and show that it captures polarization-dependent directional emission inaccessible to scalar models, while enabling the analysis of non-Markovian light-matter dynamics and entanglement. Our results provide a practical bridge between classical electromagnetic simulation tools and quantum-optical many-body and non-Markovian modeling in photonic crystal settings.
summary: This paper presents a novel constructive framework to model quantum emitters interacting with the complex electromagnetic modes of photonic crystals. By combining symmetry analysis with full Maxwell solver results, the authors derive minimal lattice Hamiltonians that overcome the limitations of existing simplified models. This allows for accurate simulation of polarization-dependent effects and non-Markovian dynamics beyond simple perturbative treatments.
main_problem: The core challenge is bridging realistic, vectorial electromagnetic descriptions of light-matter interaction in photonic crystals with computationally tractable quantum many-body models.
main_result: The authors introduce a constructive framework yielding minimal, symmetry-enforced lattice Hamiltonians that accurately reproduce the full photonic dispersion while retaining essential position and polarization dependence.
method: The method combines symmetry-constrained tight-binding constructions with numerically computed photonic band structures derived from Maxwell equations to build an effective bosonic Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum emitters coupled to a photonic crystal, modeled by deriving an effective bosonic lattice Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_B$) and coupling it to the emitter Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_S$).
key_observables: Polarization-dependent directional emission, non-Markovian light-matter dynamics, and entanglement entropy.
important_parameters: The model is analyzed in both perturbative (Born-Markov) and non-perturbative regimes; key parameters include the photonic band structure $\omega_\alpha(k)$ and coupling coefficients $g_{\alpha,k}(\mathbf{r}_i)$.
main_assumptions: Key approximations include the Born approximation, Markovian limit ($	au 	o 0$), and secular approximation when comparing to macroscopic QED results.
figures_summary: The notes mention simulations on a finite lattice using absorbing boundaries to study entanglement entropy and directional emission patterns.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the modeling trade-off, then detailing the constructive framework combining symmetry analysis with band structure calculation to derive the minimal Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_B + \hat{H}_{int}$), validating this model against Green's function/macroscopic QED results in the perturbative limit, and finally demonstrating its utility for non-Markovian dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial computational bridge, allowing researchers to use advanced quantum many-body techniques (like those used for cavity QED) on complex, structured photonic environments where simple scalar models fail.
